question: What did the two full-screen designers (🎵 Music, 🗺️ World design) do, the same way, that the rest of Dress Up's panels do not, and should every panel move to it?
how: a read-only survey of the panels' code (js/20-controls.js TABS and SHOWN_WHEN, js/22-full-screen.js, style.css), with TABS walked and SHOWN_WHEN run in node on the game's own parts at their defaults, as tools/check_load.mjs runs them; the pictures from the game in the desktop app's browser

shared: one way in, one way out
each tab's first row is a full-screen chip ("⛶ the music, full screen", "⛶ the world designer, full screen"); ✕, Escape or leaving the browser's full screen all go back
the picture's stage, the divider, the title and the 19 tabs hidden; the side panel the whole window
the tab's name and a small ✕ back, the panel's frame gone (ticket 210: the music full screen was "especially large and over-stated"; full screens "more compact, and sleek looking")
auto-fill grids, 330 px (Music) and 280 px (World) wide at least, 8 px apart; wide things span the row
the mixer's strips, and the square's things, each a card inside the card
--mu-main, --mu-mix, --mu-lfo, --mu-inst; a world square tinted by its place
a row's label hidden where the bar names the tab; the tune picker without dashed boxes
every bar, card and strip named emoji first
the grids fold to one column; the world's split, cards and in-game view only from 900 px
a knob: its label (6.2em), the slider, its value (3.8em)
the game as its first card (World)
the live picture moved into the right side's first card, sticky, folded away by its 👁️ (ticket 231)
the world's split, its view folded or not, its warnings shown or not
ticket 250 gave the Music tab outside full screen the same cards
differences: Music opens from the game's full screen (🎚️) as well as its tab; World only from its tab
Music hides the picture; World shows it as a card, from 900 px wide only
World keeps three things in the browser; Music none
unfinished: the in-game view only on windows 900 px wide or more
the 56 px bar's height written into the CSS and fitPic

stale comments (the world designer's "first piece is coming"; "the three LFOs" where there are seven; the tunes picker's dashed boxes) and two stale lines in agent-instructions.md (.world-main and .world-side; the letters "full screen only")

castle_themes.themes: A and B; each two flag colors, how they go (↔️ in turn, ▥ stripes, ▦ checkers) and a carpet; A is the castle's own, its flags outside too; B starts as A swapped; rooms take A and B in turn
castle_themes.where_set: "🎨 X's castle: its color themes", two groups of 4 rows
castle_themes.where_chosen: "🎨 its colors" (🎨 theme A / 🎨 theme B), in the box of each room with doors of its own (hallways, side, long and spiral rooms); castle N's default rooms: only the king's room
castle_themes.seen: the room's chip says "theme A" or "theme B", no colors; the colors are in another group, higher up

bubble_themes.rows: three groups (A always; B and C each with an on/off flip), five rows each: colour, size, shine, sparkle, sparkle colour
bubble_themes.where: 🏞️ Background (bubble space: 20 rows, 4 groups) and 🎮 Controls (the looks only; B and C's on/off there is blowB/blowC, apart from bubble space's bubbleBOn/bubbleCOn)
bubble_themes.flip_bug: a theme's on/off is a flip whose two labels are the same ("🅱️ theme B"), and the stylesheet shows a pressed button only inside rows and a few other places, so nothing visible changes between on and off

found: the house's 🧸 toys slider never shows

"toys" is the key of two rows (🧸 toys on the lawn, at the house; 🧸 things in the room, inside the tree house) and SHOWN_WHEN defines background.toys twice; the second (inside the tree house) wins, so at the house the slider is hidden, and inside the tree house both show, for the same setting
the bubble themes' on/off shows nothing
long labels with instructions in them
"🔭 smaller going north (% for each tenth of the picture)", "💀 skulls: biggest size (% of the usual; the smallest is the usual)", "… detail (0 = a blur, 100 = all of it)"
the bubble rows say colour; the rest of the game color
